scope: BFF composition resolver fails closed; POST /api/v1/bindings helpers restored; runtime/incident/alert idempotency moved off BFF process memory
author: Antigravity
review_status: pending independent Claude review; no approval claimed

design_choices.choice: Production resolver ends in raise UnresolvedBffDependency(name)
design_choices.why: The old catch-all lambda returned None and the stub branches returned {}, [], {'status': 'dry_run'}, a ready-True ProviderReadinessCache and fresh dicts, so a missing dependency became a silent no-op or fake success at request time. Resolution order is unchanged: explicit kwarg, loaded main attribute, explicit fallback factory, then the resolver. Real-implementation branches (auth policy, models, assistant service, personas, capital helpers, page-slice, dataset surface status, constants, owner-backed stores) are kept.

design_choices.choice: Stand-ins live in tests/bff_compose_stand_ins.py and are injected through an explicit dependency_resolver argument of compose_bff_app / mount_bff_routers / get_canonical_bff_route_set
design_choices.why: A per-call explicit argument cannot be selected by any production path; no module outside tests imports the stand-ins (asserted by test_no_production_module_imports_the_test_stand_ins). The stand-in resolver tries the production resolver first, so tests still get real implementations where they exist.

design_choices.choice: Capital helpers restored in capital/router.py (stable_capital_resource_id, capital_owner_role, raise_capital_owner_error), raise_capital_owner_error delegates to the existing _error_for_capital_exception
design_choices.why: No second error-mapping copy. The ids derive from operator+tenant+key so a retry reaches the same owner record; the owner (services/capital create_binding) replays durably by binding_id and create_capital_binding already GET-reconciles ambiguous POSTs. The BFF-local check/store cache is deleted, so the owner is the single idempotency layer. The three names are added to the runtime router dependency tuple, which is why they were previously unresolvable.

design_choices.choice: POST /bff/runtimes forwards idempotency_key to the owner's create_runtime_binding and fails closed (503 owner_idempotency_unsupported) when the owner does not accept it
design_choices.why: The only production fallback was RuntimeManagerClient.deploy, whose HTTP route has no idempotency support and a different required payload; it is removed rather than left as an un-keyed write. A binding already recorded under the same key is replayed without a second write or SSE event; any other occupied binding stays a 409. Honest consequence: until a runtime owner exposing create_runtime_binding(idempotency_key=...) is wired, this route returns 503 in production instead of writing without durable idempotency.

design_choices.choice: POST /bff/incidents derives incident_id from the key when the caller sends none, and treats an owner 409 for a matching record as a replay (mismatched title/severity -> 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT)
design_choices.why: services/incidents rejects duplicate incident_id durably, so the owner's uniqueness is the idempotency record. The BFF ledger dict is deleted.

design_choices.choice: POST /bff/alerts/{id}/acknowledge records the key + request hash + response in the durable CommandStore (foundation idempotency_record) and replays/409s from get_command_by_idempotency_key; it fails closed (503) when no durable command ledger is wired
design_choices.why: The same durable pattern command_adapters already uses. The owner write itself (status=investigating) is a set, hence naturally idempotent. Previously a command-store write failure was swallowed; it now propagates because the idempotency record is part of that write.

design_choices.choice: Deployment router gov_bff_idempotency parameter removed; incident router/service idempotency_ledger removed; ranking router capital_bff_idempotency_check/store parameters removed
design_choices.why: All were accepted and never read (the incident action ledger was write-only). Removing them deletes the literal {} at composition and the separate per-router dicts.

assertion_changes.change: The BFF-local ledger cannot exist (acceptance 5). The same-key/different-payload 409 and same-key replay assertions are kept but now run against the key-derived incident id and the owner's duplicate-id 409 (MockReadStore.create_incident now rejects duplicates like services/incidents). The old step that expected 409 for a different payload with no incident_id after an explicit-id create under the same key is replaced by the keyed flow; a key is no longer linked to an explicit client id because the incident owner has no idempotency-key field.
None. Replay and 409 assertions pass unchanged against the durable command ledger.
